The parent then only assembles them with its two resolved dependencies: BLOWUP = Submission.lpf_wtc_blowup_setIntegral_image and AREA = Submission.lpf_wtc_chart_area_formula. Both of those are still 'decomposing', so without the split nothing could be proved until they are accepted. With the split, the analytic bulk of the proof (about 90% of the Lean) can start now.

Each child is a genuine reusable obligation taken from the supplied proof:
- (fderiv_lower_bound) Step 1. If a map is differentiable at w and c-antilipschitz on an open Ω ∋ w, then c‖s‖ ≤ ‖DΦ(w)s‖.
- (gram_jacobian_continuous) Step 2. For C¹ Φ, v ↦ √det(⟨DΦ(v)eᵢ, DΦ(v)eⱼ⟩) is continuous. This is verbatim the AREA Jacobian.
- (rescaled_integral_tendsto) Steps 3(c)–6. The dominated-convergence limit (rⁿ)⁻¹∫_Ω J(v)φ(r⁻¹(Φv−Φw))dv → ∫J(w)φ(DΦ(w)s)ds, stated for any continuous weight J. The substitution v = w + rs uses Mathlib's Haar scaling and translation lemmas instead of BLOWUP on ℝⁿ, so the child needs no sibling.

How the children imply the parent. This assembly follows the supplied steps 1, 3(a), 3(b), 7 and 8.
(i) Obtain c > 0. ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ gives Continuous Φ and DifferentiableAt ℝ Φ w.
(ii) fderiv_lower_bound gives c‖s‖ ≤ ‖Ls‖, where L = fderiv ℝ Φ w. Hence:
  - L is injective;
  - finrank (LinearMap.range L.toLinearMap) = n, by LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj and finrank_euclideanSpace_fin;
  - L is c-antilipschitz on univ, via map_sub.
(iii) Fix f : C_c(ℝ^Q,ℝ). Let J be the Gram Jacobian of Φ; it is continuous by gram_jacobian_continuous. rescaled_integral_tendsto with φ = ⇑f gives Tendsto (r ↦ (rⁿ)⁻¹∫_Ω J v·f(r⁻¹•(Φv−Φw))) (𝓝[>]0) (𝓝 ∫ J w·f(L s)).
(iv) For r > 0, apply BLOWUP (S = Φ''Ω, g = f) and then AREA (h = f ∘ blowUpMap (Φw) r). This gives ∫_{blowUpMap (Φw) r '' (Φ''Ω)} f dμHE[n] = (rⁿ)⁻¹∫_Ω J v·f(r⁻¹•(Φv−Φw)).
  - h is continuous with compact support, because blowUpMap (Φw) r is definitionally (Homeomorph.subRight (Φw)).trans (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero r⁻¹ _); use HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph.
  - blowUpMap (Φw) r (Φv) = r⁻¹•(Φv−Φw) holds by rfl.
(v) Apply AREA to Ψ = ⇑L on U = univ, using L.contDiff, isOpen_univ, the antilipschitz bound from (ii), and h = f. With ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv, image_univ, Measure.restrict_univ and LinearMap.coe_range, this gives ∫_{range L} f dμHE[n] = ∫ J w·f(L s).
(vi) Tendsto.congr' on 𝓝[>]0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin) yields the second conjunct of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.

subproblems.title: Antilipschitz on an open neighbourhood gives the derivative lower bound c|s| ≤ |DΦ(w)s|
subproblems.statement: Let Q, n ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, c ∈ ℝ and w ∈ Ω. Assume Φ is differentiable at w and c|v − v′| ≤ |Φ(v) − Φ(v′)| for all v, v′ ∈ Ω. Then c|s| ≤ |DΦ(w)s| for every s ∈ ℝⁿ, where DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w and |·| is the Euclidean norm. (No sign condition on c is needed.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl Q) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (c : ℝ) (w : Eucl n), IsOpen Ω → w ∈ Ω → DifferentiableAt ℝ Φ w → (∀ v ∈ Ω, ∀ v' ∈ Ω, c * ‖v - v'‖ ≤ ‖Φ v - Φ v'‖) → ∀ s : Eucl n, c * ‖s‖ ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ Φ w s‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (lower bound for L = DΦ(w)), stated for an arbitrary real c and a map that is only differentiable at w.

Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) = Eucl P with Euclidean norm ‖·‖; L := fderiv ℝ Φ w.

1. (Setup.) Fix s ∈ ℝⁿ. Since Φ is differentiable at w, Φ has Fréchet derivative L at w (DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt).

2. (Derivative along the line.)
 - The curve ℓ(t) := w + t•s (t ∈ ℝ) has derivative s at t = 0. Lean: ((hasDerivAt_id 0).smul_const s).const_add w, after simp rewrites (1 : ℝ) • s to s.
 - ℓ(0) = w + 0•s = w, so by the chain rule γ(t) := Φ(w + t•s) has derivative L s at t = 0. Lean: HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt_of_eq 0 hline h, with h : w = w + 0•s.

3. (Slope limit.) By HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero_right, t⁻¹•(γ(0 + t) − γ(0)) → L s as t → 0 with t > 0, i.e. along the filter 𝓝[>] 0. Here γ(0 + t) = Φ(w + (0 + t)•s) and γ(0) = Φ(w + 0•s). The norm is continuous (Tendsto.norm), so ‖t⁻¹•(γ(0 + t) − γ(0))‖ → ‖L s‖ along 𝓝[>] 0.

4. (The line stays in Ω for small t.) The map t ↦ w + t•s is continuous and equals w at t = 0. Ω is open with w ∈ Ω, so Ω ∈ 𝓝 w (IsOpen.mem_nhds). Hence {t : w + t•s ∈ Ω} ∈ 𝓝 0 (ContinuousAt.preimage_mem_nhds), and it also belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (nhdsWithin_le_nhds).

5. (Inequality for small positive t.) By step 4 and self_mem_nhdsWithin, 𝓝[>]0-eventually every t satisfies t > 0 and w + t•s ∈ Ω. Fix such a t.
 - Apply the hypothesis to v := w + t•s ∈ Ω and v′ := w ∈ Ω. Since (w + t•s) − w = t•s (add_sub_cancel_left), this gives c‖t•s‖ ≤ ‖Φ(w + t•s) − Φ(w)‖.
 - Because t > 0, ‖t•s‖ = |t|·‖s‖ = t‖s‖ (norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg). So c·(t‖s‖) ≤ X, where X := ‖Φ(w + t•s) − Φ(w)‖.
 - Also ‖t⁻¹•(Φ(w + t•s) − Φ(w))‖ = t⁻¹·X, since t⁻¹ ≥ 0.
 - For t > 0, c‖s‖ ≤ t⁻¹·X ⟺ t·(c‖s‖) ≤ X (le_inv_mul_iff₀). And t·(c‖s‖) = c·(t‖s‖) ≤ X (linarith).
 - Hence, after simp rewrites 0 + t to t and 0•s to 0: c‖s‖ ≤ ‖t⁻¹•(γ(0 + t) − γ(0))‖ for 𝓝[>]0-eventually all t.

6. (Pass to the limit.) The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is nontrivial. Steps 3 and 5 give an eventual lower bound for a convergent real sequence-like family, so the bound passes to the limit (ge_of_tendsto): c‖s‖ ≤ ‖L s‖. Since s was arbitrary, c‖s‖ ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ Φ w s‖ for all s. ∎

Lean remark. The following proof was verified in the exact comparator scope as the declaration `theorem Submission.lpf_wtc_cat_fderiv_lower_bound : (<frozen statement>) := by` inside `namespace GMT.Ch06` of GMT/Ch06/Submission.lean. Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

  have hline : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => w + t • s) s 0 := by
    simpa using ((hasDerivAt_id (0 : ℝ)).smul_const s).const_add w
  have hγ : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => Φ (w + t • s)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w s) 0 := by
    have h0 : w + (0 : ℝ) • s = w := by simp
    exact hdiff.hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt_of_eq 0 hline h0.symm
  have hslope := hγ.tendsto_slope_zero_right
  have hnorm : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => ‖t⁻¹ • (Φ (w + (0 + t) • s) - Φ (w + (0 : ℝ) • s))‖)
      (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 ‖fderiv ℝ Φ w s‖) := hslope.norm
  have hcont : Continuous (fun t : ℝ => w + t • s) := continuous_const.add (continuous_id.smul continuous_const)
  have hmem : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝 (0 : ℝ), w + t • s ∈ Ω := by
    apply hcont.continuousAt.preimage_mem_nhds
    simpa using hΩ.mem_nhds hw
  have hev : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), c * ‖s‖ ≤ ‖t⁻¹ • (Φ (w + (0 + t) • s) - Φ (w + (0 : ℝ) • s))‖ := by

    have htpos : (0 : ℝ) < t := htpos
    have h1 := hanti (w + t • s) ht w hw
    simp only [zero_add, zero_smul, add_zero]
    rw [add_sub_cancel_left, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg htpos.le] at h1
    rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg (inv_nonneg.mpr htpos.le)]
    rw [le_inv_mul_iff₀ htpos]

proof_key_steps: Chain rule: γ(t) = Φ(w + t•s) has derivative DΦ(w)s at t = 0.
Slope limit: t⁻¹(Φ(w + t•s) − Φ(w)) → DΦ(w)s as t → 0+ (HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero_right), hence norms converge.
Ω open: w + t•s ∈ Ω for 𝓝[>]0-eventually all t.
Antilipschitz with v = w + t•s, v′ = w and division by t > 0: c‖s‖ ≤ ‖t⁻¹(Φ(w + t•s) − Φ(w))‖ eventually.
Pass to the limit with ge_of_tendsto: c‖s‖ ≤ ‖DΦ(w)s‖.

subproblems.title: Dominated-convergence limit of the rescaled chart integral (rⁿ)⁻¹∫_Ω J(v)φ(r⁻¹(Φ(v) − Φ(w))) dv
subproblems.statement:
Let Q, n ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q continuous, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open and w ∈ Ω. Assume Φ is differentiable at w with derivative L := DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w, and that there is c > 0 with c|v − v′| ≤ |Φ(v) − Φ(v′)| for all v, v′ ∈ Ω. Let J : ℝⁿ → ℝ be continuous and φ : ℝ^Q → ℝ continuous with compact support. Then, as r → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>] 0),
(rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_Ω J(v) φ(r⁻¹(Φ(v) − Φ(w))) dLⁿ(v) → ∫_{ℝⁿ} J(w) φ(L s) dLⁿ(s).
Here Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ and all integrals are Bochner integrals.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl Q) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (J : Eucl n → ℝ) (φ : Eucl Q → ℝ) (w : Eucl n), IsOpen Ω → w ∈ Ω → Continuous Φ → DifferentiableAt ℝ Φ w → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ v ∈ Ω, ∀ v' ∈ Ω, c * ‖v - v'‖ ≤ ‖Φ v - Φ v'‖) → Continuous J → Continuous φ → HasCompactSupport φ → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => (r ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ v in Ω, J v * φ (r⁻¹ • (Φ v - Φ w))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (∫ s, J w * φ (fderiv ℝ Φ w s)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3(c), 4, 5 and 6 of the parent proof, with J an arbitrary continuous weight (the parent uses J = JΦ). The parent's substitution v = w + rs on ℝⁿ used BLOWUP together with μHE[n] = Lⁿ. Here it is done directly with the scaling and translation formulas for Lebesgue (Haar) measure, so no sibling result is needed. The parent's step 1 limit is re-derived inside step 5 from differentiability.

Conventions: ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with Euclidean norm ‖·‖; Lⁿ = volume on Eucl n, an additive Haar measure with finrank ℝ (Eucl n) = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin); L := fderiv ℝ Φ w; B̄_ρ(x) = closedBall x ρ.

1. (Constants.)
 (a) tsupport φ is compact, hence bounded. So there is R > 0 with tsupport φ ⊆ B̄_R(0). Lean: hφc.isCompact.isBounded.subset_closedBall_lt 0 0.
 (b) φ is continuous with compact support, so there is A with ‖φ(x)‖ ≤ A for all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). Then A ≥ ‖φ(0)‖ ≥ 0.
 (c) B̄_{R/c}(w) is compact (isCompact_closedBall) and J is continuous. So there is B with ‖J(z)‖ ≤ B for all z ∈ B̄_{R/c}(w) (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). Then B ≥ ‖J(w)‖ ≥ 0, because w ∈ B̄_{R/c}(w) as R/c > 0.
 For r ∈ ℝ define k_r(v) := J(v)·φ(r⁻¹•(Φ(v) − Φ(w))) for v ∈ ℝⁿ, and F_r(s) := 1_Ω(w + r•s)·k_r(w + r•s) = Ω.indicator k_r (w + r•s) for s ∈ ℝⁿ.

2. (Change of variables v = w + r•s.) Let r > 0. Then ∫ F_r(s) ds = (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_Ω k_r(v) dv.
 - ∫_Ω k_r = ∫ Ω.indicator k_r, since Ω is open, hence measurable (integral_indicator).
 - Apply the Haar scaling formula Measure.integral_comp_smul_of_nonneg (R := r ≥ 0) to x ↦ Ω.indicator k_r (w + x). It gives ∫ Ω.indicator k_r (w + r•s) ds = (r^{finrank})⁻¹ • ∫ Ω.indicator k_r (w + x) dx, with finrank ℝ (Eucl n) = n.
 - By translation invariance (integral_add_left_eq_self), ∫ Ω.indicator k_r (w + x) dx = ∫ Ω.indicator k_r (x) dx.
 - Combining these gives the claim. All three identities hold for the Bochner integral without any integrability hypothesis.

3. (Measurability.) Fix r. k_r is continuous, as a product and composition of the continuous maps J, φ, Φ, subtraction of the constant Φ(w), and scalar multiplication by r⁻¹. Hence Ω.indicator k_r is measurable (Measurable.indicator, Ω measurable). The map s ↦ w + r•s is continuous, hence measurable. So F_r is measurable, hence AEStronglyMeasurable for Lⁿ.

4. (Domination for 0 < r ≤ 1.) Let bound(s) := 1_{B̄_{R/c}(0)}(s)·(B·A). Claim: ‖F_r(s)‖ ≤ bound(s) for all r ∈ (0, 1] and all s ∈ ℝⁿ.
 - If F_r(s) = 0 this holds because bound ≥ 0 (B, A ≥ 0).
 - Otherwise: (i) w + r•s ∈ Ω, since otherwise the indicator is 0. So F_r(s) = J(w + r•s)·φ(r⁻¹•(Φ(w + r•s) − Φ(w))).
   (ii) φ(r⁻¹•(Φ(w + r•s) − Φ(w))) ≠ 0, since otherwise F_r(s) = 0. So this point lies in support φ ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ B̄_R(0), i.e. r⁻¹‖Φ(w + r•s) − Φ(w)‖ ≤ R, i.e. ‖Φ(w + r•s) − Φ(w)‖ ≤ rR.
   (iii) The antilipschitz hypothesis with v = w + r•s ∈ Ω and v′ = w ∈ Ω gives c·r‖s‖ = c‖r•s‖ ≤ ‖Φ(w + r•s) − Φ(w)‖ ≤ rR. Dividing by r > 0 and c > 0 gives ‖s‖ ≤ R/c. So s ∈ B̄_{R/c}(0) and bound(s) = B·A.
   (iv) dist(w + r•s, w) = ‖r•s‖ = r‖s‖ ≤ ‖s‖ ≤ R/c, because 0 < r ≤ 1. Hence ‖J(w + r•s)‖ ≤ B, and ‖φ(·)‖ ≤ A.
   Therefore ‖F_r(s)‖ = ‖J(w + r•s)‖·‖φ(·)‖ ≤ B·A = bound(s).
 - bound is Lⁿ-integrable: B̄_{R/c}(0) has finite volume (measure_closedBall_lt_top), so the constant B·A is integrable on it (integrableOn_const), and its indicator is integrable (IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator, measurableSet_closedBall).
 - The set (0, 1] = Ioc 0 1 belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioc_mem_nhdsGT zero_lt_one), so the bound holds 𝓝[>]0-eventually.

5. (Pointwise limit.) Fix s ∈ ℝⁿ. We show F_t(s) → J(w)·φ(L s) as t → 0⁺.
 (i) The curve t ↦ w + t•s has derivative s at 0 and value w at 0, and Φ has derivative L at w. By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt_of_eq), γ(t) := Φ(w + t•s) has derivative L s at 0. By HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero_right, t⁻¹•(Φ(w + t•s) − Φ(w)) → L s along 𝓝[>] 0; simp removes 0 + t and 0•s.
 (ii) t ↦ w + t•s is continuous with value w at 0, so w + t•s → w along 𝓝[>] 0 (≤ 𝓝 0). Since Ω ∈ 𝓝 w (Ω open, w ∈ Ω), eventually w + t•s ∈ Ω.
 (iii) By continuity of J, J(w + t•s) → J(w). By continuity of φ and (i), φ(t⁻¹•(Φ(w + t•s) − Φ(w))) → φ(L s). Hence the product converges to J(w)·φ(L s) (Tendsto.mul).
 (iv) By (ii), for eventually all t, F_t(s) equals this product (indicator_of_mem). So F_t(s) → J(w)·φ(L s) (Tendsto.congr').

6. (Dominated convergence.) 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ) is countably generated. tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence applies with:
 - the bound function bound;
 - the eventual measurability from step 3;
 - the eventual domination and integrability of bound from step 4;
 - the pointwise limit from step 5, which holds for every s and hence a.e.
 It gives ∫ F_r(s) ds → ∫ J(w)·φ(L s) ds as r → 0⁺.

7. (Conclusion.) By step 2, for 𝓝[>]0-eventually all r (namely all r > 0, by self_mem_nhdsWithin), ∫ F_r = (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_Ω J(v)·φ(r⁻¹•(Φ(v) − Φ(w))) dv. By Tendsto.congr', the stated function converges to ∫ J(w)·φ(L s) ds = ∫ s, J w * φ (fderiv ℝ Φ w s). ∎

    exact ((hk.measurable.indicator hΩ.measurableSet).comp hlin).aestronglyMeasurable
  set bound : Eucl n → ℝ := (closedBall (0 : Eucl n) (R / c)).indicator (fun _ => B * A) with hbound
  have hdom : ∀ r : ℝ, r ∈ Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1 → ∀ s, ‖F r s‖ ≤ bound s := by
    rintro r ⟨hr0, hr1⟩ s
    by_cases hz : F r s = 0
    · rw [hz, norm_zero]
      exact indicator_nonneg (fun _ _ => mul_nonneg hB0 hA0) s
    · have hmemΩ : w + r • s ∈ Ω := by
        by_contra hnot
        exact hz (by simp only [hF, indicator_of_notMem hnot])
      have hFeq : F r s = J (w + r • s) * φ (r⁻¹ • (Φ (w + r • s) - Φ w)) := by
        simp only [hF, indicator_of_mem hmemΩ]
      have hφne : φ (r⁻¹ • (Φ (w + r • s) - Φ w)) ≠ 0 := by
        intro h0; apply hz; rw [hFeq, h0, mul_zero]
      have hinR : ‖r⁻¹ • (Φ (w + r • s) - Φ w)‖ ≤ R := by
        have := hR (subset_tsupport φ hφne)
        simpa [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right] using this
      have hΦR : ‖Φ (w + r • s) - Φ w‖ ≤ r * R := by
        rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg (inv_nonneg.mpr hr0.le), inv_mul_le_iff₀ hr0] at hinR
        exact hinR
      have hant := hcΩ (w + r • s) hmemΩ w hw
      rw [add_sub_cancel_left, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg hr0.le] at hant
      have hs : ‖s‖ ≤ R / c := by
        rw [le_div_iff₀ hc]
        have : r * (c * ‖s‖) ≤ r * R := by nlinarith
        nlinarith
      have hsball : s ∈ closedBall (0 : Eucl n) (R / c) := by
        simpa [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right] using hs
      have hwball : w + r • s ∈ closedBall w (R / c) := by
        rw [mem_closedBall, dist_eq_norm, add_sub_cancel_left, norm_smul,
          Real.norm_of_nonneg hr0.le]
        calc r * ‖s‖ ≤ 1 * ‖s‖ := by gcongr
          _ = ‖s‖ := one_mul _
          _ ≤ R / c := hs
      rw [hbound, indicator_of_mem hsball, hFeq, norm_mul]
      exact mul_le_mul (hB _ hwball) (hA _) (norm_nonneg _) hB0
  have hint : Integrable bound volume := by
    rw [hbound]
    exact (integrableOn_const (measure_closedBall_lt_top (x := (0 : Eucl n)) (r := R / c)).ne).integrable_indicator measurableSet_closedBall
  have hlim : ∀ s, Tendsto (fun r => F r s) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (J w * φ (fderiv ℝ Φ w s))) := by
    intro s
    have hline : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => w + t • s) s 0 := by
      simpa using ((hasDerivAt_id (0 : ℝ)).smul_const s).const_add w
    have hγ : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => Φ (w + t • s)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w s) 0 := by
      have h0 : w + (0 : ℝ) • s = w := by simp
      exact hdiff.hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt_of_eq 0 hline h0.symm
    have hslope : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => t⁻¹ • (Φ (w + t • s) - Φ w)) (𝓝[>] 0)
        (𝓝 (fderiv ℝ Φ w s)) := by
      simpa using hγ.tendsto_slope_zero_right
    have hcont : Continuous (fun t : ℝ => w + t • s) :=
      continuous_const.add (continuous_id.smul continuous_const)
    have hto : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => w + t • s) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 w) := by
      have := hcont.tendsto 0
      simp only [zero_smul, add_zero] at this
      exact this.mono_left nhdsWithin_le_nhds
    have hmem : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), w + t • s ∈ Ω := hto (hΩ.mem_nhds hw)
    have hJlim : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => J (w + t • s)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (J w)) :=
      (hJ.tendsto w).comp hto
    have hφlim : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => φ (t⁻¹ • (Φ (w + t • s) - Φ w))) (𝓝[>] 0)
        (𝓝 (φ (fderiv ℝ Φ w s))) := (hφ.tendsto _).comp hslope
    refine (hJlim.mul hφlim).congr' ?_
    filter_upwards [hmem] with t ht
    simp only [hF, indicator_of_mem ht]
  have hdct := tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence (μ := (volume : Measure (Eucl n)))
    (l := 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (F := F) (f := fun s => J w * φ (fderiv ℝ Φ w s)) bound
    (Eventually.of_forall hmeas)
    (by filter_upwards [Ioc_mem_nhdsGT (zero_lt_one' ℝ)] with r hr
        exact Eventually.of_forall (hdom r hr))
    hint (Eventually.of_forall hlim)
  refine hdct.congr' ?_
  filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with r hr
  exact hcov r hr
proof_key_steps: Constants: R > 0 with tsupport φ ⊆ B̄_R(0), A = sup|φ|, B = sup of |J| on B̄_{R/c}(w).
Change of variables v = w + r•s by Haar scaling and translation: (rⁿ)⁻¹∫_Ω k_r = ∫ F_r with F_r(s) = 1_Ω(w + r•s)·J(w + r•s)·φ(r⁻¹(Φ(w + r•s) − Φ(w))).
Each F_r is measurable (indicator of an open set composed with an affine map, times a continuous function).
Domination for 0 < r ≤ 1: φ ≠ 0 forces ‖Φ(w + r•s) − Φ(w)‖ ≤ rR, so the antilipschitz bound gives ‖s‖ ≤ R/c, and |F_r| ≤ B·A·1_{B̄_{R/c}(0)}, which is integrable.
Pointwise limit: eventually w + r•s ∈ Ω, slope limit r⁻¹(Φ(w + r•s) − Φ(w)) → DΦ(w)s, continuity of J and φ give F_r(s) → J(w)φ(DΦ(w)s).
Dominated convergence along the countably generated filter 𝓝[>]0, then Tendsto.congr' with the change-of-variables identity.

subproblems.title: Continuity of the Gram-determinant Jacobian √det(⟨DΦ(v)eᵢ, DΦ(v)eⱼ⟩) of a C¹ map
subproblems.statement: Let Q, n ∈ ℕ and Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q be C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ). Then the function v ↦ √det(⟨DΦ(v)eᵢ, DΦ(v)eⱼ⟩)_{i,j=1..n} is continuous on ℝⁿ. Here DΦ(v) = fderiv ℝ Φ v, eᵢ = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 are the standard basis vectors, ⟨·,·⟩ is the Euclidean inner product and √ is Real.sqrt.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl Q), ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → Continuous (fun v : Eucl n => Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin n => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ v (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ v (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (continuity of JΦ). The expression is verbatim the Jacobian of the sibling area formula.

1. (Continuity of the derivative.) Φ is C¹, i.e. ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ with order 1 ≠ 0. Hence v ↦ DΦ(v) = fderiv ℝ Φ v is continuous from ℝⁿ into the space of continuous linear maps ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ^Q with the operator-norm topology (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv).

2. (Columns.) For fixed i ∈ Fin n, v ↦ DΦ(v)eᵢ is continuous. It is evaluation of the continuous family v ↦ DΦ(v) at the constant vector eᵢ, and evaluation (A, x) ↦ A x is jointly continuous. Lean: Continuous.clm_apply with continuous_const.

3. (Gram entries.) For fixed i, j, v ↦ ⟨DΦ(v)eᵢ, DΦ(v)eⱼ⟩ is continuous, since the inner product of two continuous ℝ^Q-valued maps is continuous (Continuous.inner).

4. (Gram matrix.) An n×n real matrix is a function Fin n → Fin n → ℝ with the product topology. By step 3 and continuous_pi applied twice, v ↦ Matrix.of (fun i j => ⟨DΦ(v)eᵢ, DΦ(v)eⱼ⟩) is continuous.

5. (Determinant.) The determinant is a polynomial in the matrix entries, and ℝ is a topological ring. So v ↦ det(Matrix.of (…)) is continuous (Continuous.matrix_det).

6. (Square root.) Real.sqrt is continuous (Real.continuous_sqrt). Composing with step 5 shows v ↦ √det(⟨DΦ(v)eᵢ, DΦ(v)eⱼ⟩) is continuous. ∎

Lean remark. The following proof was verified in the exact comparator scope as `theorem Submission.lpf_wtc_cat_gram_jacobian_continuous : (<frozen statement>) := by` inside `namespace GMT.Ch06`. Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
  intro Q n Φ hΦ
  have hD : Continuous (fderiv ℝ Φ) := hΦ.continuous_fderiv (by norm_num)
  refine Real.continuous_sqrt.comp ?_
  refine Continuous.matrix_det ?_
  refine continuous_pi fun i => continuous_pi fun j => ?_
  exact (hD.clm_apply continuous_const).inner (hD.clm_apply continuous_const)
proof_key_steps: C¹ implies v ↦ fderiv ℝ Φ v is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv).
Each column v ↦ DΦ(v)eᵢ is continuous (Continuous.clm_apply), so each Gram entry is continuous (Continuous.inner).
The Gram matrix is continuous entrywise (continuous_pi twice), so its determinant is continuous (Continuous.matrix_det).
Compose with the continuous square root (Real.continuous_sqrt).
